class ApplicationRecord < ActiveRecord::Base
  primary_abstract_class
end
# A work identified by its DOI, shared by every reader who cites it. Readers'
# own annotations stay on their notes. Its metadata, and the state of the latest
# request for it, are shared too.
class Citation < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :notes, foreign_key: :citation_doi

  enum :enrichment_status, { pending: 0, completed: 1, failed: 2 }, prefix: :enrichment

  validates :doi, format: { with: %r{\A10\.\d{4,9}/\S+\z} }

  # Marks the citation pending and queues a metadata lookup, unless one is
  # already pending. Returns whether a lookup was queued. The job is queued under
  # the row lock, so a failed enqueue rolls back the pending state.
  def request_enrichment
    with_lock do
      if enrichment_pending?
        false
      else
        update!(enrichment_status: :pending, enrichment_error: nil)
        CitationEnrichmentJob.perform_later(self)
        true
      end
    end
  end

  # Asks the provider for this DOI's metadata. A permanent refusal marks the
  # enrichment failed; an unavailable provider raises so the job can retry.
  def enrich
    metadata = Provider.new.lookup(doi)
    record_enrichment(title: metadata.title, source_url: metadata.source_url, enrichment_status: :completed, enrichment_error: nil)
  rescue Provider::Error => error
    fail_enrichment(error.message)
  end

  def fail_enrichment(reason)
    record_enrichment(enrichment_status: :failed, enrichment_error: reason)
  end

  private
    # The job can load this citation before the request that queued it commits.
    # Taking the row lock waits for that commit and reloads, so the result is
    # written even when it equals the values loaded earlier.
    def record_enrichment(attributes)
      with_lock { update!(attributes) }
    end
end
# A Markdown file of one notebook's notes, written by ExportJob. The reader can
# cancel it while it is queued or working; the worker checks between notes and
# stops. A completed file can be downloaded until it expires.
class Export < ApplicationRecord
  AVAILABLE_FOR = 24.hours

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, { queued: 0, working: 1, completed: 2, cancelled: 3 }

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  def cancellable?
    queued? || working?
  end

  # Cancels a queued or working export. Returns whether it was cancelled.
  def cancel
    with_lock do
      if cancellable?
        update!(status: :cancelled)
      else
        false
      end
    end
  end

  # Writes the notebook's notes, oldest first, under its export heading. Progress
  # is saved after each note. A cancelled export stops before the next note and
  # keeps no file.
  def generate
    notes = notebook.notes.with_rich_text_body.order(:created_at, :id).to_a
    return unless start(notes.size)

    fragments = ["# #{notebook.export_heading || notebook.name}\n"]
    notes.each_with_index do |note, index|
      fragments << markdown_for(note)
      return unless record_progress(index + 1)
    end

    finish(fragments.sum)
  end

  # The authoritative check for downloading the file.
  def downloadable?
    completed? && expires_at.future?
  end

  private
    # A retried job starts again from the first note.
    def start(total)
      with_lock do
        update!(status: :working, processed_notes_count: 0, total_notes_count: total) if cancellable?
      end
    end

    def record_progress(count)
      with_lock do
        update!(processed_notes_count: count) unless cancelled?
      end
    end

    # The file is stored before the export is marked completed, so a completed
    # export always has one.
    def finish(markdown)
      blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.create_and_upload!(io: StringIO.new(markdown),
        filename: "#{notebook.slug}.md", content_type: "text/markdown")

      completed = with_lock do
        update!(file: blob, status: :completed, expires_at: AVAILABLE_FOR.from_now) unless cancelled?
      end

      blob.purge unless completed
    end

    def markdown_for(note)
      body = note.body.to_plain_text.strip
      markdown = "\n## #{note.title.squish}\n"
      markdown += "\n#{body}\n" if body.present?
      markdown
    end
end
require "csv"

# A CSV of notes for one notebook. A preview reads and validates the rows without
# saving anything. Applying validates them again and saves the import with every
# row's note, or saves nothing.
class Import < ApplicationRecord
  HEADERS = %w[ title body_html doi annotation reminder_epoch ]
  MAXIMUM_SIZE = 100.kilobytes
  MAXIMUM_ROWS = 100

  Row = Struct.new(:line, :note, :annotation)

  belongs_to :notebook
  has_many :notes, dependent: :nullify

  validate :csv_is_importable, on: :create

  # Reads one byte past the limit, which is enough to reject a larger file.
  def file=(upload)
    self.csv = String.new(upload.read(MAXIMUM_SIZE + 1).to_s, encoding: Encoding::UTF_8)
  end

  def csv
    @csv.to_s
  end

  def csv=(text)
    @csv = text.to_s
    @rows = nil
  end

  def rows
    parse unless @rows
    @rows
  end

  # The reader's annotations by source line.
  def annotations
    rows.each_with_object(ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess.new) do |row, annotations|
      annotations[row.line] = row.annotation
    end
  end

  # Validates the file and every row without saving. Returns whether the import
  # can be applied, leaving the errors on the import and each row's note.
  def preview
    valid? && rows.map { |row| row.note.valid? }.all?
  end

  def apply
    return false if invalid?

    transaction do
      save!
      rows.each do |row|
        return false unless row.note.save
      end
    end

    true
  end

  def receipt
    CSV.generate do |csv|
      csv << %w[ title doi ]
      notes.includes(:citation).order(:id).each do |note|
        citation = note.citation
        csv << [ note.title, citation && citation[:id] ]
      end
    end
  end

  private
    def parse
      @rows, @headers, @problem = [], nil, nil
      return if csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE || !csv.valid_encoding?

      reader = CSV.new(csv.delete_prefix("\uFEFF").encode(universal_newline: true))
      citations = {}
      next_line = 1

      reader.each do |fields|
        line, next_line = next_line, next_line + reader.line.count("\n")

        if @headers.nil?
          @headers = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
          break if @headers != HEADERS
        elsif fields.size != HEADERS.size && fields.any?
          @problem = "line #{line} has #{fields.size} fields instead of #{HEADERS.size}"
          break
        elsif fields.any?
          @rows << build_row(line, fields, citations)
          break if @rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        end
      end
    rescue CSV::MalformedCSVError => error
      @problem = "it is not valid CSV (#{error.message})"
    end

    # Rows naming the same DOI share one citation, so it is created only once.
    def build_row(line, fields, citations)
      title, body_html, doi, annotation, reminder_epoch = fields.map { |field| field.to_s.strip }
      citation = citations[doi] ||= Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?

      note = Note.new(notebook: notebook, import: self, title: title, body: body_html, citation: citation,
        annotation: annotation.presence, reminder_epoch: reminder_epoch.presence)

      Row.new(line, note, annotation.presence)
    end

    def csv_is_importable
      rows

      if csv.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, :blank)
      elsif csv.bytesize > MAXIMUM_SIZE
        errors.add(:csv, "must be #{ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAXIMUM_SIZE)} or smaller")
      elsif !csv.valid_encoding?
        errors.add(:csv, "must be UTF-8 text")
      elsif @problem
        errors.add(:csv, "cannot be read because #{@problem}")
      elsif @headers != HEADERS
        errors.add(:csv, "must start with the header row #{HEADERS.join(",")}")
      elsif rows.empty?
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain at least one note")
      elsif rows.size > MAXIMUM_ROWS
        errors.add(:csv, "must contain #{MAXIMUM_ROWS} notes or fewer")
      end
    end
end
class Note < ApplicationRecord
  HIGHLIGHT_COLORS = %w[ yellow green blue pink ]
  MAXIMUM_ATTACHMENT_SIZE = 1.megabyte

  belongs_to :notebook
  belongs_to :import, optional: true
  belongs_to :citation, optional: true, foreign_key: :citation_doi, validate: true
  has_rich_text :body

  enum status: { draft: 0, ready: 1 }, _prefix: true

  serialize :tags, JSON
  store_accessor :settings, :color
  alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color

  validates :title, presence: true
  validates :color, inclusion: { in: HIGHLIGHT_COLORS }, allow_blank: true
  validates :reminder_epoch, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0, less_than: 10_000_000_000 }, allow_nil: true
  validate :attachments_are_small

  scope :newest_first, -> { order(created_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :titled_like, ->(query) { where("notes.title ILIKE ?", "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query)}%") }

  def doi
    citation_doi
  end

  # Cites the shared citation with this exact DOI, ignoring surrounding whitespace.
  # A blank DOI removes the citation from the note.
  def doi=(doi)
    doi = doi.to_s.strip
    self.citation = (Citation.find_or_initialize_by(doi: doi) if doi.present?)
  end

  # The reminder time in the reader's time zone.
  def reminder_at
    Time.find_zone!(notebook.user.time_zone).at(reminder_epoch) if reminder_epoch
  end

  # Twenty-four elapsed hours after the reminder time, for postponing it a day.
  # The result keeps the reminder's UTC offset, so across a daylight saving
  # change its wall-clock time differs from the reader's local time.
  def next_day_reminder_at
    reminder_at.to_time + 86_400
  end

  def reminder_scheduled?
    reminder_job_id.present? && reminder_sent_at.nil?
  end

  # Schedules an email reminder at the given time in seconds since 1970, by
  # default the stored one, such as an imported reminder. It replaces any
  # earlier reminder for this note: the earlier job sends nothing when it runs.
  # Returns whether the reminder was scheduled. The job is queued under the row
  # lock, so a failed enqueue leaves the previous reminder in place.
  def schedule_reminder(epoch = reminder_epoch)
    with_lock do
      self.reminder_epoch = epoch

      if reminder_epoch && valid?
        job = NoteReminderJob.set(wait_until: reminder_epoch).perform_later(self)
        update!(reminder_job_id: job.job_id, reminder_sent_at: nil)
      else
        errors.add(:base, "Choose a date and time for the reminder") if reminder_epoch.nil?
        restore_attributes([:reminder_epoch])
        false
      end
    end
  end

  def postpone_reminder
    reminder_scheduled? && schedule_reminder(next_day_reminder_at.to_i)

# The configured citation metadata service. It answers GET /works?doi=... with a
# JSON title and source URL, using HTTP basic authentication. Settings come from
# config/secrets.yml, which reads them from the environment.
class Citation::Provider
  # The provider answered, but cannot supply metadata for this DOI.
  class Error < StandardError; end

  # The provider cannot answer now. Asking again later may succeed.
  class Unavailable < StandardError; end

  Metadata = Struct.new(:title, :source_url)

  def initialize(settings = Rails.application.secrets.citation_provider.to_h)
    @url, @user, @password = settings.values_at(:url, :user, :password)
  end

  def lookup(doi)
    raise Error, "No citation provider is configured" if @url.blank?

    response = connection.get("works", doi: doi)

    case response.status
    when 200 then metadata_from(response.body)
    when 401, 403 then raise Error, "The provider rejected the configured credentials (HTTP #{response.status})"
    when 404 then raise Error, "The provider has no record of this DOI"
    when 429, 500..599 then raise Unavailable, "The provider is unavailable (HTTP #{response.status})"
    else raise Error, "The provider gave an unexpected response (HTTP #{response.status})"
    end
  rescue Faraday::ConnectionFailed, Faraday::TimeoutError => error
    raise Unavailable, "The provider could not be reached (#{error.message})"
  end

  private
    # Retries a GET once on 503 before reporting the provider unavailable.
    def connection
      Faraday.new(url: @url, request: { open_timeout: 2, timeout: 5 }) do |faraday|
        faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]
        faraday.request :basic_auth, @user, @password
      end
    end

    def metadata_from(body)
      attributes = JSON.parse(body)
      title, source_url = attributes["title"], attributes["url"] if attributes.is_a?(Hash)

      if title.is_a?(String) && title.present? && web_url?(source_url)
        Metadata.new(title.strip, source_url)
      else
        raise Error, "The provider's response did not include a title and web address"
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError
      raise Error, "The provider's response was not valid JSON"
    end

    def web_url?(url)
      uri = URI.parse(url.to_s)
      uri.is_a?(URI::HTTP) && uri.host.present?
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      false
    end
end

  # Optimize range sum to use arithmetic progression if a block is not given and
  # we have a range of numeric values.
  def sum(initial_value = 0)
    if block_given? || !(first.is_a?(Integer) && last.is_a?(Integer))
      super
    else

      if actual_last >= first

class DigestMailer < ApplicationMailer
  # Lists the reader's ready notes last updated on the day of the request.
  # Active Job deserializes the request time in the worker's time zone (UTC),
  # so that is the day the digest covers, which can differ from the reader's
  # local day near midnight.
  def daily_digest
    @reader, requested_at = params.values_at(:reader, :requested_at)
    @date = requested_at.to_date
    @notes = @reader.notes.status_ready.where(updated_at: requested_at.all_day).includes(:notebook).order(:updated_at, :id)
    @completion = BigDecimal(params[:completion])

    mail to: @reader.email, subject: "Your reading digest for #{l @date, format: :long}"
  end
end

content.text:
I found 6 high-risk changes, 6 medium and 6 low in the upgrade from Rails 7.0.8.7 to 8.1.0. The most serious ones change behaviour without raising an error, so the test suite may not show them. Several others (removal of `Rails.application.secrets`, and the old `enum`, `serialize` and `alias_attribute` forms) stop the app from booting, so they show up straight away.

I unpacked activesupport, activerecord, activejob, actiontext, actionpack, actionview, activemodel and railties at both versions under `/tmp/g/` and compared their source. I did not install anything or run the app.

Each claim is tagged: **[code]** means I read it in the gem or app source, **[changelog]** means a Rails changelog, and **[inference]** means my own reasoning.

## Facts about the app that the ratings depend on

Please correct any that are wrong.
- `config.load_defaults 7.0` is set, and none of the framework defaults from 7.1 to 8.1 have been adopted (`config/application.rb:12`).
- The database is PostgreSQL through `pg` 1.6.0.
- Assets use Sprockets with importmap, Turbo and Stimulus. Pages are rendered as HTML, and Jbuilder is also installed.
- Active Job runs on Sidekiq **6.5.12** using Rails's built-in `:sidekiq` adapter, with `redis` 4.8.1. One job, `ExportJob`, is a plain Sidekiq job.
- Action Text and Active Storage (Disk service) are in use, and Action Cable uses Redis in production.
- Settings come from `config/secrets.yml` through `Rails.application.secrets`.
- Ruby 3.3.6 meets Rails 8.1's minimum of 3.2. The pinned `concurrent-ruby` 1.3.4 meets the new minimum of 1.3.1. The pinned `minitest ~> 5.25` still satisfies Rails 8.1's requirement (minitest >= 5.1).
- **[inference]** I assumed web and Sidekiq processes are deployed together but can overlap during a rollout, and that jobs are still queued in Redis at that moment.

## High risk

**1. Job time arguments now arrive in the sender's time zone, which changes what the daily digest contains** [code]
- **Before (7.0):** a time-with-zone argument was rebuilt in the worker's time zone, `Time.iso8601(value).in_time_zone`.
- **Now (8.1):** the job stores the zone name and rebuilds the time in it (`activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/serializers/time_with_zone_serializer.rb`).
- **Where the app uses it:** `app/models/user.rb:38` passes `Time.current.in_time_zone(time_zone)` to `DigestJob`. `app/mailers/digest_mailer.rb:8-9` then uses `requested_at.to_date` and `requested_at.all_day` and relies on the time being in UTC, as its own comment says.
- **What goes wrong:** with no error, the digest covers the reader's local day instead of the UTC day, so a different set of notes is selected near midnight.
- **Tests to recheck:** `test/controllers/digests_controller_test.rb:10,39`.
- Introduced in Rails 7.1 ([7-1-stable activejob CHANGELOG](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md)).

**2. BigDecimal job arguments are now wrapped in a serializer, and old workers can't read them** [code]
- **Before:** BigDecimal was passed through as a plain value (`activejob-7.0.8.7/lib/active_job/arguments.rb:50`), so Sidekiq's JSON stored it as a string.
- **Now:** it is wrapped by `BigDecimalSerializer`.
- **Where the app uses it:** `user.rb:38` passes `reading_completion`. `DigestMailer` calls `BigDecimal(params[:completion])`, which works with either form.
- **What goes wrong:** during the rollout, a 7.0 worker that picks up an 8.1-queued digest raises `Serializer ActiveJob::Serializers::BigDecimalSerializer is not known` (`activejob-7.0.8.7/lib/active_job/serializers.rb:43`), and that digest is lost.

**3. `wait: :exponentially_longer` was removed, and the job only fails when it retries** [code]
- **Where the app uses it:** `app/jobs/citation_enrichment_job.rb:7`.
- **Now:** the 8.1 `determine_delay` only knows `:polynomially_longer` and raises `Couldn't determine a delay` for anything else (`activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/exceptions.rb:175-188`).
- **What goes wrong:**
  - Booting succeeds; the error only fires on the first `Provider::Unavailable`.
  - The `fail_enrichment` block never runs, Sidekiq's own retries take over, and the citation can stay `pending`.
  - Because `request_enrichment` refuses to queue again while the citation is pending, it also stops new lookups.
- **Fix:** rename to `:polynomially_longer`, which uses the same formula. Deprecated in 7.1 and removed in 7.2.

**4. `citation[:id]` no longer returns the primary key** [code]
- **Before (7.0):** `read_attribute` mapped `"id"` to the primary key (`activerecord-7.0.8.7/.../read.rb:31`).
- **Now (8.1):** that mapping is gone.
- **Where the app uses it:** `citations` uses `doi` as its primary key and has no `id` column (`db/schema.rb:55`). `app/models/import.rb:72` writes `citation[:id]` into the import receipt CSV.
- **What goes wrong:** **[inference]** the DOI column of the receipt silently becomes empty.
- **Fix:** use `citation.doi` or `citation.id`.

**5. `TimeWithZone#to_time` now always keeps the time zone** [code]
- **Where the app uses it:** `app/models/note.rb:44` builds the next-day reminder with `reminder_at.to_time + 86_400`.
- **Before:** under the 7.0 defaults, `to_time` kept the UTC offset.
- **Now:** it calls `getlocal(time_zone)` (`time_with_zone.rb:497`).
- **Effect:**
  - **[inference]** The stored epoch (`.to_i`) is the same either way.
  - The displayed time and `iso8601` value in `app/views/notes/_reminder.html.erb:19` will now show the post-DST offset across a daylight-saving change.
  - This contradicts the model comment at `note.rb:41-43`. Severity is low, but it is a silent change in time handling.

**6. The Sidekiq adapter is deprecated, and Sidekiq 6.5 is untested with Rails 8**
- **Deprecation [code]:** 8.1's built-in adapter warns that it "will be removed in Rails 8.2" and asks for Sidekiq 7.3.3 or later (`activejob-8.1.0/.../sidekiq_adapter.rb`).
- **Compatibility [inference]:** Sidekiq 6.5.12 and Rails 8.1 are not a combination I know to be tested, and moving to Sidekiq 7 also requires redis-client and changes the Redis API.
- **App code that depends on Sidekiq/Redis directly:** `user.rb:37-44` (`Sidekiq.redis` `sadd`, which returns a boolean in redis 4.x) and `notebook.rb:25-29` (`perform_async`, `Redis::BaseError`).
- Treat this as a separate upgrade that has to be planned.

## Medium risk

**7. `Rails.application.secrets` is removed** [code]
- railties 8.1 no longer defines it; it was removed in 7.2.
- **Used in:** `app/models/citation/provider.rb:13`, and the test that changes it at `test/controllers/citation_enrichments_controller_test.rb:45,117-122`.
- **Decision needed:** move these settings to credentials, to `config_for(:citation_provider)`, or to environment variables. `config/secrets.yml` is ignored after the upgrade.

**8. `ActionText::ContentHelper.allowed_tags` now defaults to `nil`** [code]
- Before, it defaulted to an array (actiontext 7.0 `content_helper.rb:8`). Now the full list is computed in `sanitizer_allowed_tags`.
- **Used in:** `config/initializers/action_text.rb` runs `allowed_tags += %w[details summary]`, which becomes `nil + [...]` and raises `NoMethodError`.
- **What could go wrong:** **[inference]** the obvious fix, `= %w[details summary]`, would silently strip every other formatting tag. The list has to be built from `sanitizer.class.allowed_tags + [attachment tag, "figure", "figcaption"] + %w[details summary]`.
- **Test to recheck:** `test/controllers/notes_controller_test.rb:137`.

**9. `serialize :preferences` with no coder** (`app/models/notebook.rb:8`) [code]
- It keeps working under `load_defaults 7.0`, which still uses YAML.
- Adopting the 7.1 defaults sets `default_column_serializer = nil`, and then this line raises "missing keyword: :coder" (`railties-8.1.0/.../configuration.rb:287`).
- **Decision needed:** keep YAML with `coder: YAML`, or migrate the data stored in the column.

**10. `attr_readonly :slug`** (`notebook.rb:9`) [code]
- The 7.1 default `raise_on_assign_to_attr_readonly = true` (`configuration.rb:284`) makes assigning to `slug` raise instead of being silently ignored.
- **Decision needed:** this only applies if you adopt that default.

**11. PostgreSQL date decoding** [code]
- Rails 8.1 adds `decode_dates`, which defaults to off but is turned on by the 7.2 framework defaults (`configuration.rb:332`).
- **Used in:** `app/models/notebook.rb:40` passes the raw `select_rows` value to `Date.iso8601`.
- **What could go wrong:** with the setting on, the value is already a `Date`, so that call raises a `TypeError`.

**12. Rails 8.2 will remove the deprecations now being warned about**
- This includes the Sidekiq adapter and the `to_time_preserves_timezone` setting.
- Production has `report_deprecations = false`, so check the deprecation warnings in development and test.

## Low risk

These fail loudly at boot or in tests.
- **`enum status: {...}, _prefix: true`** (`app/models/note.rb:10`): the keyword form is removed. Write `enum :status, {...}, prefix: true` [code].
- **`serialize :tags, JSON`** (`note.rb:12`): passing the coder as a positional argument is removed. Write `coder: JSON` [code].
- **`alias_attribute :highlight_color, :color`** (`note.rb:14`): `color` is a `store_accessor`, not a column attribute, and 8.x raises `ArgumentError` when an alias points at one (`activerecord-8.1.0/.../attribute_methods.rb:91`). Use `alias_method` for the reader and the writer [code].
- **`fragments.sum`** (`app/models/export.rb:42`): Active Support no longer lets `sum` add strings, so this raises `TypeError` in `ExportJob`. Use `fragments.join` [code].
- **`set(wait_until: reminder_epoch)` with an integer** (`note.rb:58`):
  - **Before:** 7.0 called `.to_f` on the value.
  - **Now:** 8.1 stores it as given, then calls `scheduled_at.utc` while serializing the job, which raises `NoMethodError` on an Integer (`activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/core.rb:130,177`).
  - **Fix:** pass `Time.at(epoch)` [code].
- **`config.cache_classes`** (`config/environments/*.rb`): it still works, but the newer name is `enable_reloading` [inference].

## Parts judged not relevant

- **MySQL, SQLite and Trilogy adapters, and Solid Queue/Cache/Cable defaults:** the app uses PostgreSQL, Sidekiq and Redis.
- **Propshaft as the new default:** existing Sprockets apps keep `sprockets-rails` [inference].
- **`enqueue_after_transaction_commit`:**
  - In 8.1 it is `false` (`activejob-8.1.0/lib/active_job/enqueuing.rb:53`), so the queue-under-row-lock design in `citation.rb:17-25` and `note.rb:54-66` is unaffected.
  - Do not turn it on, because those methods rely on a failed enqueue rolling back.
- **Native Sidekiq `ExportJob`:** it doesn't go through Active Job, so none of the changes above affect it.
- **`has_secure_password`, `form_with` and `button_to`:** I found no changes relevant to how the app uses them, but I didn't diff these exhaustively [inference].
- **Action Cable:** the app has only the default channel scaffolding.

Most of these were introduced in Rails 7.1 and 7.2, so the full entries are in those series' changelogs (the 8.1.0 gems only include the 8.x changelog): https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-1-stable/activejob/CHANGELOG.md, https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/activerecord/CHANGELOG.md and https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/7-2-stable/railties/CHANGELOG.md.
